subtitle: Crypto doesn't trade in a vacuum. When DXY rises, when VIX spikes, when S&P 500 futures fall — crypto reacts within hours. The macro stack tells you the GLOBAL risk environment that determines whether crypto setups are likely to work or fail.

blocks.content:
You've built complete chart-reading skills, indicator mastery, and advanced concepts. Tier 5 zooms out: what's happening in the BROADER financial world that affects crypto?

Crypto is a risk asset. When global risk appetite goes up, crypto tends to rally. When global risk-off hits (war scare, rate hike surprise, banking crisis), crypto often falls WITH (or harder than) equities. Knowing the macro stack tells you when your chart setups have a tailwind vs a headwind.
The four key macro indicators

rows: Strength of USD vs basket of major currencies
INVERSE — strong dollar = pressure on crypto (and other assets priced in USD)
INVERSE typically — VIX spike = risk-off = crypto sells. Sometimes decouples in crypto-specific events.
POSITIVE — when ES rallies, crypto often follows. When ES falls, crypto often falls harder.
Long-term US interest rate; risk-free rate
Generally INVERSE for risk assets — rising yields make crypto less attractive

blocks.content: The risk-on / risk-off framework

blocks.title: Two macro regimes that matter most
blocks.content:
RISK-ON: investors comfortable, looking for returns. Equities rally, crypto rallies, yields stable or falling, DXY weak, VIX low.

RISK-OFF: fear dominates, investors run to safety. Equities sell, crypto sells (often harder), yields fall (flight to bonds), DXY spikes, VIX spikes.

In risk-off, ALL risk assets fall together regardless of individual stories. Your perfect BTC technical setup means nothing if the global tape is in risk-off — the broader flow overrides individual chart signals.
The hierarchy of correlation

In risk events, risk assets fall in a predictable order:

  1. Tech/growth stocks (NASDAQ futures, QQQ) — high-beta to risk; fall first.
  2. BTC + ETH — closely follow the move; often slightly delayed.
  3. Major alts (SOL, BNB, XRP, AVAX) — fall in line with BTC but amplified (1.5-2x BTC's move).
  4. Mid-cap alts — amplified further (2-3x BTC's move).
  5. Small-cap alts — wildest moves; can fall 30-50% in a few hours during severe risk-off.

This hierarchy means: when you see equity tech rolling over, you have a head-start signal that crypto pain is coming. Especially for high-leverage alt longs, equity weakness is your early warning.
DXY in detail

The US Dollar Index (DXY) measures USD strength vs EUR, JPY, GBP, CAD, SEK, CHF (weighted). Why it matters for crypto:

  • Crypto is priced in USD. Strong USD = relative weakness in crypto's USD price even if crypto's intrinsic value is unchanged.
  • USD strength reflects global flight-to-safety. Same dynamic that pushes investors INTO USD pushes them OUT of risk assets.
  • Many crypto correlations operate through DXY. ETH-USD weakness during DXY rallies isn't ETH-specific; it's USD-specific.

Watch DXY when crypto is in a key technical zone. If DXY is rallying (e.g., approaching 105+), expect downward pressure on crypto. If DXY is falling (e.g., breaking below 100), expect tailwind for crypto.
VIX and what spikes mean
VIX measures implied volatility on S&P 500 options. It's known as the 'fear gauge' because it spikes when investors are buying puts (insurance against decline):

rows: Crypto can grind higher; risk-on environment
No strong macro signal; trade technicals
Risk-off in progress; tighten crypto longs, consider reducing leverage
Severe risk-off; crypto often crashes 10-20%; defensive posturing critical

blocks.title: VIX above 30 = different market
blocks.content:
When VIX spikes above 30, normal technical setups stop working. Liquidity dries up, correlations spike toward 1 (everything moves together), and volatility regimes change. Your beautiful S/R levels can break by 5-10% on a single candle as flight-to-cash dynamics dominate.

During VIX > 30 environments: reduce leverage, widen stops (or sit out), don't try to fade volatility. These are environments to SURVIVE, not to maximize on. Wait for VIX to normalize before resuming aggressive setups.
S&P 500 futures (ES) as the lead indicator

ES (S&P 500 e-mini futures) trades nearly 24/7 and often LEADS crypto by minutes to hours during risk events. When equities open and fall sharply, crypto typically follows within the hour.

Practical: have an ES chart visible alongside your BTC chart during US market hours (14:30-21:00 UTC). When ES breaks key levels or shows strong directional moves, crypto reacts quickly.

  • ES strong rally + crypto setup bullish = aligned, high-conviction long
  • ES strong sell-off + crypto setup bullish = conflicting; the macro flow usually wins
  • ES neutral or sideways + crypto setup = trade the crypto technicals normally
When crypto decouples

Crypto isn't always correlated to equities. Periods of decoupling include:

  • Crypto-specific news (major ETF approval, regulatory news, exchange failure).
  • Halving cycles when crypto-specific supply dynamics dominate.
  • When crypto is in deep markdown — already crashed below where it 'should' be relative to equities.
  • Bull markets when retail crypto FOMO temporarily decouples from equity correlation.

Decoupling isn't permanent. Eventually the correlation reasserts. But during decoupling phases, crypto-specific setups dominate macro signals.
Practical macro check workflow

1. Before any crypto trade, glance at the macro stack: DXY level + trend, VIX level, ES today's action.
  2. Classify the macro regime: clearly risk-on, clearly risk-off, or neutral?
  3. Match your crypto bias to the regime. Bullish crypto setups + risk-on = aligned, higher quality. Bullish crypto + risk-off = conflicting, lower quality (or skip).
  4. Reduce leverage during VIX spikes. Even high-conviction setups can be steamrolled by macro flows.
  5. Watch ES during US hours as a lead indicator for crypto direction.
Worked example

Setup: BTC has a clean bullish setup on 4H — pullback to support, hammer candle, volume, RSI bullish divergence. Looks like A+ long.

Macro check:

  • DXY at 103 and rallying hard (broke 102 resistance with momentum)
  • VIX at 27 (elevated)
  • ES selling off, breaking below 200 SMA on daily

The macro is CLEARLY risk-off. Despite the beautiful BTC setup, the broader environment is hostile.

Smart decision: REDUCE size by half (or skip), use tighter SL, take partial profits faster. The setup might still work — but the probability is meaningfully lower than the same setup during risk-on.

Alternatively, you could wait for the macro to stabilize (DXY pulls back, VIX falls below 20, ES stabilizes) and revisit the BTC setup then. The technicals will often re-form once macro headwinds ease.

blocks.title: Take this with you
blocks.content:
Three rules:

  1. Check the macro stack before every trade. DXY, VIX, ES. 30 seconds.
  2. Match crypto bias to macro regime. Aligned = higher quality. Conflicting = reduce size or skip.
  3. VIX above 30 = different market. Survive, don't maximize. Wait for normalization before aggressive setups.
